title: Optimize: Control Plane API + Webhook Contract for Safe, Idempotent Cost Recommendations
creator: Ava Patel
description: Provide a hardened control-plane API and webhook contract to enable Optimize automation to safely propose, apply, and roll back batching and caching configuration changes. Goals: (1) guarantee idempotent apply operations so retries and duplicate webhook deliveries never produce duplicate state changes, (2) define a compact, versioned webhook schema with tamper protection and replay resistance, (3) expose preview and dry-run endpoints for SDKs and console workflows, and (4) ensure rollback and canary semantics are first-class. This ticket covers API surface design, server-side idempotency semantics, webhook delivery guarantees, and SDK helper primitives for clients to perform safe applies and rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: API endpoints exist: POST /v1/optimize/recs/preview, POST /v1/optimize/recs/commit, POST /v1/optimize/recs/rollback, GET /v1/optimize/recs/:id
All commit endpoints accept an operation_id (client-generated) and enforce at-least-once-safe semantics: repeated requests with same operation_id are deduplicated and return the original result
Webhooks delivered to customer endpoints include X-Optimize-Signature and X-Optimize-Idempotency headers; signature verification documented and works with KMS-backed HMAC keys
A preview mode returns estimated cost delta, tokenized delta heatmap for affected routes, and a stable rec id for commit/rollback
Server-side apply supports conflict detection against current runtime config and returns structured conflict details for SDK to surface
Rollback endpoint can accept either rec id or operation_id and is idempotent
End-to-end integration tests cover duplicate commit attempts, replayed webhook deliveries, failed partial apply with automatic revert, and manual rollback flows
Documentation and SDK helpers added for JS/Python clients demonstrating common safe patterns (generate operation_id, validate webhook signature, perform dry-run then commit)
Security review sign-off on webhook signing, key rotation, and replay protection completed
implementation_notes: Use operation_id UUIDv4 provided by SDK/console; server stores (operation_id -> apply_result) for 30 days by default
Implement optimistic compare-and-swap on runtime config version/tags to detect concurrent changes; return 409 with current_version & diff when conflicts occur
Persist rec proposals and apply metadata in Optimize control-plane DB with strong consistency for idempotency guarantees
Expose a preview response with cost_estimate_usd, qps_impact_estimate, and per-route token delta sample (strings with small arrays) to keep contracts compact
Webhook signature: HMAC-SHA256 over the canonicalized JSON body + timestamp header; include signature_version and key_id headers to support rotation
Retry semantics: webhook delivery is at-least-once from our side; customers should use idempotency header to deduplicate. We'll support exponential backoff with jitter for retries
Limit apply to bounded operations: reject proposals that change >50% of routes in a single apply without explicit 'bulk_overrides' flag
Observability: emit trace/span with request.operation_id, control_plane_version, and runtime_config_version; link to console rollout view
api_contract: Design summary: endpoints and minimal payloads (v1). POST /v1/optimize/recs/preview accepts {proposal: {...}, operation_id, options:{dry_run:true}} and returns {rec_id, operation_id, cost_estimate_usd, token_delta_summary, preview_version}. POST /v1/optimize/recs/commit accepts {rec_id | operation_id, requester, apply_mode: [canary|immediate], canary_pct, reason} and returns {rec_id, status: queued|applied|conflict, apply_result}. GET /v1/optimize/recs/:id returns current status, diff, and timeline. POST /v1/optimize/recs/rollback accepts {rec_id | operation_id, reason, operation_id} and returns {rollback_id, status}. All write endpoints require idempotency via operation_id header or body field. Error model includes 409 conflict, 422 validation, 401/403 auth errors. Authentication: bearer tokens tied to API keys and scopes (optimize:write, optimize:read).
webhook_contract: Webhook summary: one topic 'optimize.recommendation.update'. Delivery: POST to customer endpoint with JSON body of {rec_id, operation_id, event_type: [preview|commit|apply_result|rollback], status, summary, timestamp}. Headers: X-Optimize-Signature: sha256=..., X-Optimize-Timestamp: unix-ms, X-Optimize-Key-Id: key-xxx, X-Optimize-Idempotency: operation_id. Signature algorithm: HMAC-SHA256 over (timestamp + '.' + body). Signature verification docs and pseudo-code provided in Confluence. Webhook payloads are versioned (v1) and include a 'links' array of strings for console/GH artifacts. Delivery guarantees: at-least-once; we will retry up to 72 hours with exponential backoff. Customers should dedupe by X-Optimize-Idempotency. Failure handling: on repeated 5xx/timeout we will mark subscription unhealthy and escalate to customer via email/console alert after threshold
rollout_plan: API proto and mock servers implemented behind feature flag in staging
SDK helpers for JS/Python add operation_id generation + signature helpers (PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js#124, sdk-py#89)
Canary rollout to 5 internal customers (optimize-internal team) with monitoring dashboard for cost delta and apply success rate
Gradual enablement for all hosted Optimize customers over 3 weeks with forced dry-run followed by optional commit
Post-rollout 2-week hypercare and runbook for rollback and incident communication
testing_plan: Unit tests for idempotency store and dedupe logic (including clock skew scenarios)
Integration tests: preview -> commit -> simulated duplicate commit -> verify single apply
E2E harness to validate signature verification, replayed webhook deliveries, and failed midway apply with automatic rollback
Chaos tests that force concurrent config updates to validate conflict detection and safe failure modes
Security tests for signature/key rotation and expired timestamp rejection
